fix.summary: Fixed the ten design-system findings inside packages/ui and the shared common.json catalogue. Four pure, dependency-free modules fell out of the fixes and now own the rules that were previously guessed per-component: `contrast.ts` (WCAG luminance/ratio maths, reproduces every audit number to 2dp), `layers.ts` (the single stacking order + `resolveToastLayer`), `toast-policy.ts` (severity → duration/politeness + pausable timer arithmetic) and `ui-strings.tsx` (the design system's own accessible names). frontend-05 was settled by measurement, not by a z-index bump: I served the real styles.css in a browser and found that a toast promoted with `showPopover()` *before* a dialog opens is still painted under `.lbr-modal::backdrop` (top-layer paint order is entry order) and only a re-promotion *after* the dialog joined paints above it — and that in all cases the toast is inert, because a modal dialog blocks hit-testing outside its own subtree. So the fix is two-sided: the stack re-promotes itself into the top layer (Modal/HelpDrawer report in through a tiny registry in layers.ts), and Modal gained an `error` slot that renders a focused critical Banner inside the dialog, where the librarian can actually interact with it. Verified in the browser against the real stylesheet: 0 duplicate title ids (was 3), 0 spurious banner landmarks (was 3), footer legal links 44px on a coarse pointer (was 17px), `--color-warning-text` resolving to the computed #8e6400. Verified by running the pure modules: 38 assertions pass, including CSS/TS parity on the z-index scale and a check that no ad-hoc z-index literal survives anywhere in styles.css. `npx tsc --noEmit` in packages/ui, `pnpm check:translations` and `prettier --check` are all clean. No repo-root turbo commands were run and nothing outside my two paths was touched.

findings_addressed.what_changed: New packages/ui/src/layers.ts owns the whole stacking order: a named z-index scale (sticky 50 / popover 55 / scrim 60 / drawer 70 / toast 80) mirrored into a `:root` `--lbr-z-*` block in styles.css, so no component invents a number again (the old literal 9000 and the four inline literals are gone; a check asserts no z-index literal outside the scale remains in the stylesheet). Because `showModal()` beats every z-index, ToastProvider promotes the stack into the browser top layer with `popover="manual"`, driven by the pure `resolveToastLayer()` resolver. I measured the three orderings in a browser against the real styles.css: no popover = toast dimmed behind the backdrop; popover shown BEFORE the dialog = still dimmed (top-layer paint order is entry order); re-promoted AFTER the dialog = painted crisply above. Hence Modal and HelpDrawer call `registerOpenModal()` so the stack knows to re-promote. The same measurements showed `elementFromPoint()` at the toast's close button returns the dialog in ALL cases — a modal makes everything outside its subtree inert, so a toast over an open dialog can be read but never clicked. That is a platform rule, so Modal also gained an `error?: ReactNode` prop that renders a focused `<Banner severity="critical">` inside the dialog body (`.lbr-modal__error`), which is where a mid-task failure belongs.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: The apps/web half is not mine: apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx:152-157 still only toasts on the ApiError path and never closes or reports in the dialog. It now needs one line — pass the message to `<Modal error={...}>` — and the same for BookDetail, MemberDetail, BarcodeScanner and the data-model editors. Also: if a toast is already visible and the user then opens a modal, that toast stays dimmed until the next toast arrives; re-promotion is driven by the toast list changing plus the modal registry, and I chose not to add a document-wide MutationObserver for that edge.

findings_addressed.what_changed: Modal and HelpDrawer derive their title id from `React.useId()` (`${instanceId}-title`) instead of the hardcoded `lbr-modal-title` / `lbr-help-drawer-title`. Verified in a browser repro reproducing LoanActions' three-modals-mounted-at-once structure: `document.querySelectorAll('#lbr-modal-title').length` is 0 where the audit measured 3, and each dialog's `aria-labelledby` now resolves to its own heading. Modal also sets `aria-describedby` at the error slot when one is present.

Replaced the English defaults with a `UiStringsProvider` / `useUiStrings()` context in the new ui-strings.tsx, plus `uiStringsFromCatalog(t)` which maps the `UiStrings` shape onto real catalogue ids so a caller cannot get a key name wrong. Toast finally has a label at all (`ToastItem.dismissLabel`, defaulting to the shared string) instead of a hardcoded `aria-label="Dismiss"`; Modal `closeLabel`, HelpDrawer `closeLabel`, HelpButton `ariaLabel` and ConfirmDestructive's four English literals ("This cannot be undone.", "Type X to confirm", the case-insensitivity hint, "Delete forever") all fall back to it. Banner cannot use context (it renders inside server components), so its type is now a discriminated union that makes `dismissLabel` REQUIRED whenever `onDismiss` is passed — the TypeScript forcing function the finding asked for, which breaks nothing because the one existing call site already passes both. Added 13 keys to both catalogs. Every UiStrings member is a plain string, deliberately: functions cannot cross the Next server/client boundary, so the two strings needing a runtime value carry an invisible marker finished by `splitAroundMarker`/`fillMarker` at render.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: apps/web must mount `<UiStringsProvider strings={uiStringsFromCatalog(t)}>` ABOVE each `<ToastProvider>` (4 sites: app/[locale]/admin/layout.tsx:36 and app/[locale]/t/[slug]/layout.tsx:89/121/135/189) or the labels stay on their English fallback; `useUiStrings` logs a one-time dev warning when no provider is found, so the gap is loud rather than silent. Combobox.tsx and DataTable.tsx are in apps/web — I see the concurrent agent has already routed Combobox's 'Could not search.' through a client translator; DataTable's 'Something went wrong. Try again.' can use the `common.table.loadFailed` key I added.

findings_addressed.what_changed: Shipped the computation the branding flow lacks, as pure functions: `checkBrandColor(hex)` returns the more readable of the two foreground tokens, the button ratio, the ratio of the colour used as text on the app surface, and a pass/fail for each — because `--color-primary` is a button background AND link/active-nav text. Also `readableForeground()` (which foreground token to flip `--color-primary-fg` to) and `toAccessibleTextColor()`. It reproduces the audit's numbers exactly: #ffd60a 1.41, #ffffff 1.00, #4cc9f0 1.92, #90ee90 1.42.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: Enforcement lives in files I do not own. apps/api/src/branding/branding.controller.ts:43-47 still validates only `HEX.test()` — it should reject or auto-flip when `checkBrandColor(...).passesAsButton` is false; apps/web BrandingForm.tsx should show the live warning, and layout.tsx should set `--color-primary-fg` from `readableForeground(brandColor)`. @libriant/ui is a React package, so if apps/api cannot import it the ~40 lines of contrast.ts should be lifted rather than re-derived.

findings_addressed.what_changed: Banner maps `severity="critical"` to `role="alert"` (assertive, announced on insertion) and keeps `role="status"` for the rest, with a caller override still possible. The toast stack is now a named region (`aria-label` from `ui.notifications`) rather than an anonymous `role="region"`. Critical toasts carry `role="alert"`; non-critical toasts deliberately carry no role at all, so they are announced once by the stack's persistent polite region instead of nesting a second live region inside it. Modal moves focus to its error slot when one appears, which covers the 'no focus move on failure' half for every dialog.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: The page-level half is apps/web: LoginForm.tsx:64-71 still neither moves focus nor writes into a permanently-mounted region on a failed submit, and the same pattern is on the loans, plans, support-access and announcement pages. Banner accepts `tabIndex`/`ref` through its rest props, so that is a small change at each site.

findings_addressed.what_changed: The doc comment promised hover-to-pause and the code had no handler; both are now real. New toast-policy.ts holds the durations — info/success 5s, warning 10s, critical STICKY (`null`) so an error never expires unread — and a pause/resume timer as four pure functions. Pointing at or tabbing into the stack pauses every running timer; leaving resumes with the time that was left, not a fresh 5s and not a lost one (verified across two pause/resume cycles). A toast arriving while the stack is already hovered starts paused. Timers are cleared on unmount, which the old fire-and-forget `void handle` never did. An explicit `durationMs` from the caller still wins, including an explicit number on a critical. The lying doc comment is rewritten to describe what the code does.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: No toast history/recall was added — sticky errors plus pause address SC 2.2.1, but a dismissed confirmation is still unrecoverable. No apps/web call site passes `durationMs`, so the new severity defaults apply everywhere immediately.

findings_addressed.what_changed: FormField's `cloneElement` now injects `'aria-required': required ? true : undefined` alongside id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid, and the child prop type was widened to accept it. Chose `aria-required` over the native `required` attribute so the browser's own validation bubble does not fight the app's inline error handling. The `aria-hidden` asterisk stays as the visual cue.

`<header>`/`<footer>` inside Modal and HelpDrawer became `<div>`s — the class names already carried all the styling. Verified in a browser repro with three modals mounted as LoanActions does: `document.querySelectorAll('header').length` is 0 (the audit's accessibility tree reported a `banner` landmark per dialog) and only the page's own `<footer>` remains.

The defective file is apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx, which I do not own and which the concurrent agent is editing right now — so I built the corrected primitive where it belongs, as packages/ui/src/Combobox.tsx, exported from @libriant/ui. It is presentational (the caller keeps query state, debouncing and fetching), and it fixes all three defects: `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` track the *rendered* listbox rather than an internal `open` flag, so a focused empty field no longer reports an expanded popup with a dangling `aria-controls`; the listbox contains nothing but `role="option"` children, with loading/error/no-matches moved to a sibling `.lbr-combobox__status` panel (error carries `role="alert"` there, where it is legal); and a permanently-mounted visually-hidden live region reports the result count, mounted empty and filled later. Added the strings it needs (`combobox.searching`, `combobox.searchFailed`, `combobox.results.one`/`.other`) to both catalogs.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: The live defect is unfixed until apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx is replaced by (or wraps) this primitive — a mechanical swap that lifts query state into the caller. Until then the design system carries two comboboxes; I would treat the app copy as the thing to delete, not a second implementation to maintain.

findings_addressed.what_changed: Added `.lbr-legal-links__item` and `.lbr-powered-by` to the existing `@media (pointer: coarse)` block with `min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center`. Measured in a browser at 375x812 with touch emulation: all four legal links and the CyberSystema attribution now report 44px tall (the audit measured 17px and 16px), and they are unchanged at 17px on a fine pointer, which is correct — SC 2.5.8 targets coarse input.

Not on my assigned list, but the styles.css half is in my ownership so I did it. Dropped the `opacity` dimming from `.lbr-landing__eyebrow`, `.lbr-landing__hero-sub` and `.lbr-landing__hero-note`: computed with the new `flatten()`, white on the brand gradient goes from 3.79/3.98/3.80 and 4.34/4.55/4.32 to 4.63/4.85/4.61 — AA at both gradient ends and the midpoint. Verified resolving in a browser.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: The three text usages are in apps/web and still reference `var(--color-warning)`: LoansTable.tsx:81 (the overdue marker), settings/activity/AuditLog.tsx:97 and staff/StaffManager.tsx:209. frontend-16's enforcement points are apps/api/src/branding/branding.controller.ts and apps/web BrandingForm/layout, all outside my ownership. Delivered checkBrandColor/readableForeground in packages/ui/src/contrast.ts; nothing rejects a 1.41:1 brand colour yet.

frontend-13 is only half-effective until apps/web mounts <UiStringsProvider> above its four <ToastProvider>s. Left a one-time dev console warning from useUiStrings so the omission is visible rather than silent.

frontend-05's toast is visible over an open dialog but not clickable — a modal dialog blocks hit-testing outside its subtree, confirmed by measurement in three configurations. No design-system change can route around that; Modal's new inline `error` slot is the answer, and apps/web must use it.

No frontend test runner exists (frontend-29), so I could not add regression tests. The four new modules are pure and dependency-free for exactly that reason, and I exercised them with 38 ad-hoc assertions via tsx (scratchpad only, not committed) covering the layer resolver, the pause/resume arithmetic, CSS/TS parity on the z-index scale, and the Greek catalogue round-trip.

verdicts.reasoning: The design-system mechanics are real and I reproduced them in a browser (served packages/ui/src/styles.css over http, drove showModal()/showPopover() from JS): a popover promoted AFTER the dialog paints crisply above .lbr-modal::backdrop, one promoted BEFORE it is still dimmed underneath — so resolveToastLayer's 'repromote' rule and the layers.ts modal registry are justified, and the --lbr-z-* scale is genuinely the only source of z-index in styles.css (grep: every z-index is var(--lbr-z-*)). But the finding is 'the error toast is invisible AND unclickable AND the modal never closes'. I measured document.elementFromPoint() at the toast's close button returning the <dialog> and c.focus() failing (document.activeElement !== the button) in ALL dialog-open configurations including the re-promoted one — the toast is inert, exactly as the report concedes. The answer the report offers for that, Modal's new `error` slot, has ZERO call sites: apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx is byte-identical on the ApiError path (line ~156 still `toast.show({severity:'critical', ...})` with no setOpenModal(null) and no error= prop on ReturnModal/RenewModal/MarkLostModal), and no file in apps/web passes `error=` to a Modal. So the librarian's experience is unchanged except that the critical toast is now sticky and visible-but-dead behind the modal. Design-system half done, live defect intact.
verdicts.bypass: None — this is an incomplete fix, not an evasion. The measurements in the report are honest and I independently reproduced them.

verdicts.reasoning: Modal.tsx:68-70 derives `const instanceId = React.useId(); const titleId = `${instanceId}-title``, and both aria-labelledby (line ~103) and the <h2 id={titleId}> use it; HelpDrawer.tsx:39 does the same. grep across packages/ui/src/*.tsx returns zero `id="lbr` literals and zero occurrences of 'lbr-modal-title'/'lbr-help-drawer-title' outside doc comments. React.useId is SSR-safe by construction (server and client walk the same tree and produce the same `:R…:` ids), so this is not the hand-rolled-counter hydration trap the brief warned about, and `npx tsc --noEmit` in apps/web is clean so no call site broke. The new aria-describedby={error ? errorId : undefined} points at a div that renders under exactly the same condition, so no dangling idref was introduced. Verified end-to-end: Modal is the component the three LoanActions dialogs use, so the duplicate-id condition is genuinely gone.

Nothing a Greek librarian hears has changed. `grep -rn 'UiStringsProvider|uiStringsFromCatalog' apps/web` returns ZERO hits — the provider is mounted nowhere, so useUiStrings() falls through to defaultUiStrings and every control still announces 'Close', 'Dismiss', 'Notifications', 'Show help for this page', 'Close help', 'This cannot be undone.', 'Delete forever'. The plumbing is sound (catalogue ids are `common.actions.close`-style, which matches packages/i18n/src/catalog.ts's 'namespaces are folders merged into namespace.key ids'; all 13 keys exist in BOTH locales and `pnpm check:translations` passes; the {text}/{count} placeholders line up with format()'s regex and splitAroundMarker/fillMarker round-trip correctly). Banner's discriminated union does force dismissLabel, and the sole call site (apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/EmailVerifyBanner.tsx:62-63) already passes it. But the finding is about what users hear, and that is 100% unchanged. Note also that the two sighted-user strings the finding named were fixed by the CONCURRENT agent (apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:93 and DataTable.tsx now use translateApiError), not by this work — the `common.table.loadFailed` key added here is unreferenced.
verdicts.bypass: The claimed forcing function is one-sided: `useUiStrings` logs a dev-only console.warn instead of failing, so a build or CI run gives no signal that the provider is missing. The English defaults the finding asked to REMOVE were kept, just relocated into defaultUiStrings — which is the same 'optional prop with an English default is a string that will be English forever' failure mode the module's own doc comment condemns.

verdicts.reasoning: apps/api/src/branding/branding.controller.ts is untouched (`git diff --stat -- apps/api/src/branding/` is empty); setColor still does only `HEX.test(body.brandColor)`. Nothing rejects or corrects a 1.41:1 colour, and BrandingForm/layout.tsx still never set --color-primary-fg from the picked colour. Worse, the enforcement recipe the report hands off is wrong: I ran checkBrandColor('#ffd60a') and got `{foreground:'#0d1117', ratio:13.40, ratioAsText:1.41, passesAsButton:TRUE, passesAsText:false}`, because readableForeground() silently flips the foreground to near-black. So 'reject or auto-flip when checkBrandColor(...).passesAsButton is false' — the exact instruction in the residual-risk note — would NOT fire for the audit's own worked example. The guard only works if a caller separately applies the returned `foreground` to --color-primary-fg, which nothing does. The maths itself is correct: I reproduced 1.41 / 1.00 / 1.92 / 1.42 exactly, and meets() is a strict unrounded `>= target` (meets(4.4996) === false, meets(4.5) === true), so there is no round-up-at-the-boundary bug.

Half of the downgraded finding is done and done correctly: Banner.tsx:38 maps severity 'critical' to role='alert' with a caller override, the toast stack has an accessible name (aria-label={ui.notifications}), and liveRegionRoleFor() gives critical toasts role='alert' while leaving the rest roleless so they are announced once by the stack's polite region — that nesting reasoning is right (the nearest ancestor with aria-live wins, so no double-announce). The other half is untouched: apps/web/app/[locale]/login/LoginForm.tsx still mounts the Banner conditionally and handleSubmit still never moves focus, and the same is true on loans/plans/support-access/announcements. Modal's focus-the-error effect is the stated substitute and, as under frontend-05, has zero call sites. Also note that role='alert' inside a modal dialog is moot for the toast path: I measured the whole stack as inert while a dialog is open, and inert subtrees are dropped from the accessibility tree, so a critical toast fired from a modal is announced to nobody regardless of the popover promotion.
verdicts.bypass: None deliberate, but the report's framing — 'Modal moves focus to its error slot, which covers the no-focus-move-on-failure half for every dialog' — is not true of any shipped page, since no dialog passes `error`.

verdicts.reasoning: This one is real and live, because ToastProvider is mounted app-wide. The doc comment now matches the code. I ran the pure timer functions: a 5000ms toast paused at t=2000 reports 3000ms left, resumed at 10000 still 3000, paused again at 11000 reports 2000, resumed at 60000 counts down 2000/1000/0 — no reset, no loss, correct across two cycles. Sticky (null) returns null forever. resolveDuration honours an explicit number on a critical (1000) and an explicit null on a success. Defaults are info/success 5000, warning 10000, critical null. In the component: onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave and onFocus/onBlur (React's focusin/focusout, so focus-within works) drive setPaused; a toast arriving while paused is paused at birth (Toast.tsx: `if (pausedRef.current) state = pauseTimer(state, now)`); and the unmount effect clears every handle, which the old `void handle` never did. SC 2.2.1 is genuinely addressed. See the regressions list for the sticky-stack overflow this introduces.

FormField.tsx cloneElement now injects `'aria-required': required ? true : undefined` alongside id/aria-describedby/aria-invalid, and the child prop type was widened to accept `'aria-required'?: boolean | 'true' | 'false'`. Input/Textarea spread `...rest` onto the native element so the attribute lands. aria-required over the native `required` is the right call for forms that do their own validation. The aria-hidden asterisk stays as the visual cue, which is correct. apps/web typechecks clean, so every existing FormField child accepts the new prop.

Modal.tsx now renders `<div className="lbr-modal__header">` and `<div className="lbr-modal__actions">`; HelpDrawer.tsx renders `<div className="lbr-help-drawer__header">`. `grep -n '<header|<footer' packages/ui/src/*.tsx` leaves only PageHeader.tsx:30, which is not a dialog and sits inside <main> (an element on the HTML-AAM exception list), so it does not add a banner landmark. All the styling is class-based — I checked styles.css for element-qualified selectors like `header.lbr-modal__header` and there are none, and the mobile override at :1596 targets `.lbr-modal__header` by class — so nothing visual regressed.

The defective file is untouched. apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx still has, verbatim: `aria-expanded={open}` and unconditional `aria-controls={listboxId}` on the input, against `{open && query.trim().length >= minQueryChars ?
    `; and inside that listbox, `
  • ` for loading/no-matches plus `
  • {error}
    • ` for the error. All three defects the finding names are live. The new packages/ui/src/Combobox.tsx is correct in isolation (aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-activedescendant all keyed to `listboxVisible`, listbox children are all role='option', status panel is a sibling, permanently-mounted visually-hidden role='status' for the count, and .lbr-combobox__status / .lbr-visually-hidden both exist in styles.css) — but it is imported by nothing and is now exported from the @libriant/ui barrel alongside the app's divergent copy.

styles.css:1573-1577 adds `.lbr-legal-links__item, .lbr-powered-by { min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }` inside the existing `@media (pointer: coarse)` block. I checked the two ways this could silently not apply and neither bites: (1) `.lbr-legal-links__item`'s base rule at :1677 comes AFTER the media block but sets only color/font-size/text-decoration, so there is no later same-specificity `display` to win; (2) `.lbr-powered-by` has no stylesheet rule at all — its display:inline-flex/align-items:center come from an inline `style` attribute in PoweredBy.tsx, which would beat the CSS, but they are the same values and min-height is NOT set inline, so the 44px applies. Both are already flex items or inline-flex, so min-height maps to real box height. Fine-pointer rendering is untouched, which is correct for SC 2.5.8.

regressions.issue: Critical toasts are now sticky (durationMs null) but .lbr-toast-stack (styles.css:655-663) has no max-height, no overflow scrolling and no cap on item count. apps/web/components/OfflineQueueProvider.tsx fires one critical toast PER failed or expired queued action inside a for-loop (lines ~100 'loans.queue.expired' and ~145 'loans.queue.syncFailed'). Before this change each vanished after 5s; now a librarian who queued ten actions offline and reconnects to ten conflicts gets ten permanent toasts stacking upward from bottom-right, each needing a manual click. The column grows past the top of the viewport with overflow:visible on a position:fixed element, so the oldest ones are unreachable and un-dismissable, and the whole column blocks clicks on the right-hand side of the page until dismissed one by one. This is the exact scenario the finding cited as the motivation for stickiness, so the sticky default is right — but it needs a stack cap, a max-height with overflow-y:auto, or coalescing.

The error-focus effect is `React.useEffect(() => { if (open && error) errorRef.current?.focus(); }, [open, error])` where `error` is typed `React.ReactNode`. A caller who passes JSX rather than a plain string — e.g. `error={<>{msg} retry}`, which the prop's own type invites — creates a new object identity on every render, so the effect re-runs every render and yanks focus out of whatever input the librarian is typing into inside the dialog. The documented use case (a mid-task failure in a form dialog) is precisely where this bites. Latent today because no call site passes `error`; it will fire the first time one does. Depend on a stable key instead (e.g. a boolean `hasError` plus an explicit error id/nonce).

checkBrandColor('#ffd60a') returns passesAsButton: TRUE (13.40:1) because readableForeground() flips the foreground token to #0d1117 before measuring. The report's own hand-off instruction — 'apps/api branding.controller.ts should reject or auto-flip when checkBrandColor(...).passesAsButton is false' — therefore does nothing for the audit's worked example, and for #90ee90, #4cc9f0 and every other pale brand colour. Whoever implements the guard from that sentence will ship a no-op. The verdict object needs either a passesWithCurrentForeground field measured against the fixed #ffffff the app actually renders, or the doc must state that honouring the returned `foreground` is mandatory, not optional.

pausedRef is a latch cleared only by mouseleave/focusout on the stack. Hovering the stack and clicking the last toast's × shrinks the stack to a zero-size box under the cursor without reliably firing mouseleave, so pausedRef stays true; the next toast is then born paused (`if (pausedRef.current) state = pauseTimer(state, now)`) and never auto-dismisses until some later pointer movement produces a mouseleave. Self-healing in practice, but it means 'confirmations expire' is not guaranteed. Reconciling paused state against a real hover/focus check when the item list empties would close it.

New, fully-implemented, zero-import component exported from the @libriant/ui barrel (index.ts:7) while apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx — the one actually rendered by checkout and place-hold — keeps all three ARIA defects. Two divergent comboboxes now ship, and `import { Combobox } from '@libriant/ui'` vs `from '@/components/Combobox'` differ silently in accessibility behaviour and in whether the caller owns query state.

verify.overall:
Four of ten genuinely fixed end-to-end (frontend-12, -22, -23, -24, plus -26 = five); five are design-system-only and leave the user-visible defect intact (frontend-05, -13, -16, -20, -25).

What holds up. The work is unusually honest — every claim I could check reproduced. I served the real styles.css over http and drove the top-layer scenarios from JS: a popover promoted AFTER showModal() paints crisply above .lbr-modal::backdrop, one promoted BEFORE it stays dimmed underneath, and elementFromPoint plus a focus() probe confirm the stack is inert in every dialog-open configuration. The contrast module reproduces 1.41 / 1.00 / 1.92 / 1.42 and #8e6400, and meets() is a strict unrounded >= (meets(4.4996) is false), so there is no boundary round-up bug. The pause/resume arithmetic is correct across two cycles with no reset and no loss. React.useId is the right SSR-safe primitive and no hydration trap was introduced. All 13 catalogue keys exist in both el and en with matching placeholders, pnpm check:translations passes, and npx tsc --noEmit is clean in BOTH packages/ui and apps/web — the Banner discriminated union breaks nothing because the one onDismiss call site (EmailVerifyBanner.tsx:62) already passes dismissLabel. No z-index literal survives in styles.css. The frontend-26 CSS survives both specificity traps I looked for.

Where it does not reach. Three of the five partials are blocked on the same thing: nothing in apps/web adopts the new API. `grep -rn UiStringsProvider apps/web` is empty, so every label a Greek librarian hears is still the English fallback (frontend-13). No Modal anywhere passes `error=`, and LoanActions' ApiError path is byte-identical — still toast-only, still leaves the dialog open (frontend-05, and the focus half of frontend-20). apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx retains all three ARIA defects verbatim (frontend-25). branding.controller.ts is untouched (frontend-16).

Two things I would not merge as-is. Sticky criticals with no cap on the stack turn the offline-queue replay loop into ten permanent, partly off-screen toasts — the fix's own motivating scenario, made worse in a different way. And Modal's error-focus effect depends on a ReactNode, so the first caller who passes JSX will steal focus on every keystroke. Both are cheap to close.

One framing correction worth carrying forward: the report says a toast over an open dialog "can be read but never clicked". For a screen-reader user it cannot be read either — the stack is inert, and inert subtrees leave the accessibility tree, so the promoted-popover work buys sighted users visibility and buys AT users nothing. That strengthens rather than weakens the case for Modal's inline error slot, which is the piece that still needs wiring.

resilience.summary: All 11 web-app resilience and localisation findings addressed in apps/web/** and locales/* (common.json untouched). The app now has a failure story: three error boundaries (global / locale / tenant-page) that render branded, localized, retryable screens from a build-time-bundled catalogue; every fetch has a defensible deadline (10 s interactive, 60 s job) and a typed ApiUnavailableError; the maintenance takeover reaches signed-in users because currentImpersonation() and currentSystemMode() now fail soft and the system mode resolves before anything that can reject; ~50 call sites that rendered the API's hardcoded English now go through translateApiError(), backed by 30 new errors.json keys covering network/timeout, every HTTP status class, plan-gate 402s and quota ceilings. Also: sign-out plus a support address on both billing-gate screens; an in-app language switch on the sidebar, both auth cards, the verify-email page and the landing page, persisted in a libriant_locale cookie and honoured by `/` and the offline page, with login now landing on the tenant's own defaultLocale; a skip link + id="lbr-main" on the tenant and admin shells and a catalogued nav landmark; hero opacity raised to 1.0 and a new --color-warning-text (#7c5e00, 6.07:1 vs 3.14:1) for the overdue marker and the small warning labels; a fully localised verify-email flow whose dead end is escapable without email delivery; a bilingual offline page and a localised 404. Verified: apps/web `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint apps/web` clean, `prettier --check` clean, `check-translations` passes, and translateApiError smoke-tested against 14 failure shapes in both locales.

findings_addressed.what_changed: Added apps/web/app/global-error.tsx (self-contained document, catches throws from the locale layout itself), apps/web/app/[locale]/error.tsx (branded outage screen with illustrations/outage, reset() retry and a home link) and apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/error.tsx (page-level, keeps the sidebar so only the broken page is lost). Copy comes from new system.crash.* keys in both catalogues via lib/static-catalog.ts, which imports the system+errors JSON at build time — an error boundary gets no props and must not fetch its own copy during an outage. Separately fixed the trigger: currentSession() now short-circuits on hasSessionCookie() instead of firing /auth/me for any cookie at all, and /login and /signup use a new optionalSession() that swallows every failure so the sign-in form renders during an API outage.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: global-error.tsx starts in Greek and corrects the locale in a mount effect (the root layout that would parse the URL is what failed); an English reader sees Greek for one frame.

findings_addressed.what_changed: lib/impersonation.ts now returns null on ANY error (an unreadable impersonation probe is not an impersonation) — it used to rethrow the 503 that /support/impersonation/me returns during maintenance, since that path is not on the middleware's ALWAYS_PASS list. lib/system-mode.ts now resolves out_of_order for every failure, not just ApiError — a raw fetch rejection means we could not reach the control plane at all, a stronger outage signal than a 5xx. The tenant layout resolves the system mode alone and first, no longer inside a Promise.all with the impersonation probe, so nothing that can reject is awaited before the takeover branch is evaluated.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: A partial outage where /system-mode/current answers 'normal' but /auth/me 5xxs still throws — it now lands on the branded, retryable [locale]/error.tsx rather than a bare 500.

findings_addressed.what_changed: lib/api.ts sets init.signal = AbortSignal.timeout(...) on every request. Two documented classes: API_TIMEOUT_MS (10 s, overridable via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_TIMEOUT_MS) for anything a person is waiting on — above the slowest healthy request, short enough to fail while the librarian is still watching instead of reloading and piling on more hung renders; API_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS (60 s) for work that legitimately runs before answering, applied to the CSV validate/commit POST and to the four multipart uploads that bypass api() (import, branding logo, book cover, member photo). Both the fetch and the body read are wrapped, and failures become a typed ApiUnavailableError with reason 'timeout' | 'network' that translateApiError renders as a distinct localized message. The tenant layout's billing and desktop gate catches were widened to tolerate it so a wedged API degrades exactly like a 503.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: A server render still makes up to four sequential api() calls, so the worst case is ~40 s rather than 10 s (previously 4x300 s). A timed-out circulation write is classified 'offline' and queued; the existing idempotency key makes the replay safe.

findings_addressed.what_changed: New lib/api-errors.ts exports translateApiError(err, t, fallback?), which never returns err.message: it prefers errors.api.<code> when the API sends a code, then handles 402 (PlanGuard/QuotaInterceptor bodies -> quotaExceeded.description with a translated feature noun, or planFeature.named) and 503 (maintenance middleware's reason -> read-only / maintenance / unavailable), then maps by status, then falls back to the caller's contextual message or errors.generic.*. The API's English text is logged to the console in dev where an operator wants it. 30 new keys per locale in errors.json (network.timeout/unreachable, http.*, planFeature.*, quotaExceeded.descriptionUnnamed, feature.* for all 15 feature keys). Routed ~50 tenant-facing call sites through it, plus billing/page.tsx's Promise.allSettled reason and OfflineQueueProvider's sync-failure toast, and gave DataTable and Combobox a locale-derived translator so their failures are localized without threading a prop through every caller.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: Specific API detail is lost: a 400 now reads 'Some of the details weren't accepted' in Greek instead of 'Due date must be after the checkout date' in English. The real fix is machine codes on the API side, which I cannot touch — translateApiError already prefers errors.api.<code>, so wiring it later needs only new catalogue keys, no web changes. The 32 admin-plane files and ImpersonationBanner.tsx were deliberately left on err.message: they are English-only screens for Libriant staff, and translating one line of an otherwise wholly English banner would read worse than leaving it.

findings_addressed.what_changed: verify-email/page.tsx, VerifyEmailClient.tsx and EmailVerifyBanner.tsx are fully localised from 19 new auth.verifyEmail.* keys per locale; the page and banner take catalog+locale from their callers. Replaced both <Link><Button> nestings with styled anchors (a <button> inside an <a> is invalid HTML and gives two focus stops). The dead end is now escapable without assuming mail is delivered: the banner is dismissible for the session, its copy says what to do if nothing arrives, and both the banner and the verify page's failure state carry a mailto:hello@libriant.com route to a human who can confirm the address. The resend toast says a link is on its way rather than claiming it landed in the inbox.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: The web app still cannot detect EMAIL_DRIVER=console — /auth/me does not surface it and apps/api is owned by another workflow. The fix is honest copy plus a human fallback rather than a driver-aware banner.

findings_addressed.what_changed: The non-admin plan-gate notice in the tenant layout now renders a LogoutButton and a contact link (t('billing.actions.contactSales') -> mailto:hello@libriant.com), and ChoosePlanScreen grew a LogoutButton in its footer — mirroring DesktopGate, the takeover that already got this right. There is no GET logout route, so without the button the only exit was clearing cookies, which also strands the admin who needs to sign in at the same circulation desk.

Placed in the tenant sidebar footer, on the login, signup and verify-email cards, and swapped in on the landing page so a click there is remembered too. app/page.tsx now honours the cookie before negotiateLocale(accept-language), which short-circuits to 'en' for any en-* tag. Did not run a production `next build`: packages/ui currently has six TypeScript errors from the concurrent UI-kit work (Combobox.tsx:148, ConfirmDestructive.tsx:69, ui-strings.tsx:86 and :95), which would fail the build for reasons outside this change. apps/web's own `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. Heads-up on a possible collision: the UI-kit agent added common.combobox.searchFailed and common.table.loadFailed to common.json and there is now a packages/ui/src/Combobox.tsx. If those components are being replaced by UI-kit versions, my two files may become dead code.

fix.summary: Localised the Electron shell's two English-only surfaces — the bundled offline/setup page and the custom menu — into el/en with Greek as the default. The desktop app has no i18n access of its own and cannot get one: `@libriant/i18n` is an ESM TypeScript *source* package and `/locales/**` is read off the Next server's filesystem, while the shell is a CommonJS `tsc` bundle whose installer ships only `dist/`, `static/` and `package.json` (electron-builder `files`), and the fallback page is a `file://` page with no network and no fetch. So I added a small locale resolution in the main process (`apps/desktop/src/i18n.ts`) holding the menu strings in the same flat el/en shape as `/locales/<lang>/*.json`, and inlined the page strings in `static/fallback.html`; both are documented as ready to move to `locales/{el,en}/desktop.json` if packaging ever carries them. Menu labels key off `app.getLocale()` — deliberately the same source Electron localises its `role` items from, which is what stops the bar being half-and-half (`LIBRIANT_LOCALE` overrides). The offline page gets its locale from the main process via a `?lang=` query param, preferring the locale in the URL the librarian was actually on (`/<locale>/…`) and falling back to the OS one. `main.ts` no longer hands the page an English sentence for the repeated-crash case — it passes `reason=crashed` and the page words it. The raw Chromium code is no longer the message: recognised codes (DNS, offline, refused/timed-out/reset, cert/SSL) get a Greek/English explanation and the `ERR_…` string is demoted to a labelled "Τεχνική λεπτομέρεια" line for support. Greek matches the register of the neighbouring catalogs (formal plural, "Παρακαλούμε/Δοκιμάστε ξανά", "πρόγραμμα περιήγησης", "διακομιστής"). I did NOT touch `DEFAULT_APP_URL` — the audit itself downgraded that half of the finding as a known-state DNS gap, and repointing it would be a deployment decision, not a fix.

findings_addressed.what_changed: New apps/desktop/src/i18n.ts: SUPPORTED_LOCALES/DEFAULT_LOCALE mirroring @libriant/i18n (Greek default), localeFromTag() using the same base-subtag rule as negotiateLocale(), localeFromUrl() reading the /<locale>/… prefix every Libriant route carries, a lazily-cached uiLocale() (LIBRIANT_LOCALE > app.getLocale() > el) and t(). All eight custom menu labels in main.ts (View, Connection, Reload from server, Safe mode…, Open config folder…, Reset to default server, Check for updates…, Open logs…) now go through t(), so they follow the same OS locale Electron localises its role items from. loadFallback() gained a reason ('unreachable' | 'crashed') and passes lang= to the page instead of an English sentence; the render-process-gone path no longer sends 'The app crashed repeatedly.'. static/fallback.html: <html lang> is now el with the Greek copy written into the markup (so a script that never runs still leaves a Greek page), plus an inline el/en catalog the script applies — heading, body, URL label, the three buttons, the status line, the bridge-unavailable message, and the ack/failure strings. Raw ERR_ codes are mapped to a plain-language sentence (name-not-resolved, internet-disconnected, connection-*/timed-out/address-unreachable, ERR_CERT*/ERR_SSL*) with the raw string kept as a labelled technical detail. Greek-parity is enforced at compile time: the EL map is typed Record<MessageKey, string>, so an EN key without a Greek one fails typecheck (proved by removing one key — TS2741 — then restoring). README documents the language behaviour and why the strings do not live in /locales.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: Two catalogs (main process + page) instead of one shared file, because neither surface can read /locales in a packaged build — they use identical shapes so a later move to locales/{el,en}/desktop.json is mechanical, and pnpm check:translations does not cover them. Electron still renders the role-based items (File/Edit/Window/Help/appMenu) itself: the bar is now internally consistent because our labels use the same OS locale, but a Greek library running an English Windows gets an all-English menu unless LIBRIANT_LOCALE=el is set (documented in the README). apps/desktop has no test runner (the test script is a stub), so verification was typecheck + eslint + prettier + rendering fallback.html in a browser for el/en, unreachable/crashed, several ERR_ codes, and a bogus lang value.

out_of_scope_files_needed: /Users/leontgmusic/Projects/libriant/docs/audit/pre-release-2026-08-23/remediation/STATE.json — frontend-09 needs marking as remediated; another workflow is editing this file right now, so I left it alone.

/Users/leontgmusic/Projects/libriant/locales/el/desktop.json and /Users/leontgmusic/Projects/libriant/locales/en/desktop.json — OPTIONAL follow-up if the team wants the 8 menu keys under pnpm check:translations instead of in apps/desktop/src/i18n.ts. It only pays off together with a packaging change (electron-builder extraResources copying locales/{el,en}/desktop.json into the bundle) plus a build step, since the packaged main process ships only dist/ + static/ + package.json; the fallback page still could not read them (file://, no fetch). I chose not to ask for it: it buys catalog parity at the cost of a fragile cross-package packaging dependency for 8 strings, and the type-level EL parity gate covers the same drift.
/Users/leontgmusic/Projects/libriant/locales/{el,en}/*.json — NOT needed for this change; I added no keys to the shared catalogs, so check:translations parity is untouched by me.

That is the same half-localized class and the file is inside apps/desktop, but localizing it needs CFBundleLocalizations + el.lproj/InfoPlist.strings shipped via extraFiles, and I cannot run electron-builder here to verify the packaged bundle, so I did not risk breaking packaging blind.

DEFAULT_APP_URL (apps/desktop/src/config.ts:11) still points at https://app.libriant.com, which has no DNS record. Deliberately untouched: the audit's own verdict downgraded that as a known state, and both suggested remedies (repoint the default, or bake the tenant URL into the installer served by /t/:slug/desktop) are deployment/API-side decisions outside apps/desktop.

verdicts.reasoning: VERIFIED by execution, not just by reading. (1) Every user-visible string on the fallback page is resolved at runtime in BOTH locales, not merely defined: I extracted the inline script from apps/desktop/static/fallback.html and ran it in a Node VM against a stub DOM for 10 query-param combinations. el/en both render heading, body, urlLabel, connect, retry, browser, title and <html lang> correctly; reason=crashed swaps to crashedHeading/crashedBody and hides the technical-detail box; ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED / ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED / ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID map to plain-language sentences with the raw code demoted behind a localized 'Τεχνική λεπτομέρεια:' / 'Technical detail:' label; an unrecognised code falls back to the generic body; lang=__proto__ and a param-less load both land on Greek (allowlist compare at fallback.html:344, not an index lookup) rather than a blank page. The three click handlers were exercised too: invalid URL -> 'Δεν εφαρμόστηκε: μη έγκυρη διεύθυνση', empty -> 'Εισαγάγετε τη διεύθυνση του διακομιστή.', retry -> 'Νέα προσπάθεια…'. All nine element ids referenced by setText/getElementById exist in the markup, so no silent throw. (2) The locale is determined by something real: I loaded the compiled i18n.js with a stubbed electron module — uiLocale() returns el for el-GR, en for en-US, honours LIBRIANT_LOCALE, and degrades to DEFAULT_LOCALE='el' for de-DE, garbage and '' ; and localeFromUrl() correctly reads el/en from /<locale>/… , returns null for '/', 'not a url', file:// and /t/acme. The premise that every route is locale-prefixed is real (apps/web/app/[locale]/ plus apps/web/app/page.tsx redirecting / to /${negotiateLocale(accept)}). The cache is not poisoned pre-ready: buildMenu() is called inside app.whenReady().then() at main.ts:557-561, so app.getLocale() is already reliable when uiLocale() first runs. (3) The packaged build still has access to the catalog. This was the most likely way for the fix to break in the installer and it does not: tsconfig include is src/**/*.ts, so i18n.ts compiles into dist/ (I emitted to a scratch outDir and saw dist/i18n.js plus `const i18n_js_1 = require("./i18n.js")` in main.js — correct CommonJS interop under NodeNext with no "type":"module"), and electron-builder.yml files: is `dist/**/*`, `static/**/*`, `package.json`. Nothing reads /locales, node_modules, or any dev-only path at runtime; the page strings are inline in a file:// document. The Greek copy is also written into the static markup, so a script that never runs still leaves a Greek page rather than an English one. (4) No new hazards: the fallback page's Connect/Retry genuinely work because isTrustedSender explicitly trusts file:// (main.ts:107), so the localized ack strings are reachable rather than dead code; check:translations only walks /locales so parity CI is unaffected; npx tsc --noEmit exits 0; eslint --max-warnings 0 and prettier --check are clean on all four files. Greek-parity is genuinely gated at compile time (EL typed Record<MessageKey,string>). Grepping the repo shows the old English literals ('Reload from server', "Can't reach Libriant", 'Desktop bridge unavailable') now survive only inside the en catalogs. The one part of the original finding left undone — DEFAULT_APP_URL at apps/desktop/src/config.ts:11 — is exactly the half the audit's own verdict downgraded as a known-state DNS gap, so leaving it is consistent with the record rather than a gap in the remediation.
verdicts.bypass: The claimed invariant 'the menu bar is no longer half-and-half' holds only when the OS UI language is el or en. On any third locale (verified with de-DE) uiLocale() falls to DEFAULT_LOCALE='el' while Electron localizes its role items (File/Edit/Window/Help) into German — a German-plus-Greek bar. It is not worse than the pre-fix German-plus-English bar and is irrelevant to a Greek-only customer base, but the invariant as stated in the report is false outside {el,en}.

regressions.issue: uiLocale() collapses every unsupported OS locale to DEFAULT_LOCALE ('el'), but Electron's role-based menu items (appMenu/fileMenu/editMenu/windowMenu/help) are localized by Chromium into that OS language. Verified with a stubbed app.getLocale()='de-DE': the custom labels come back Greek while the role items would render German, so the mixed-language menu bar the finding describes still occurs off the el/en axis. Not worse than before the fix (it was German + English) and harmless for the Greek-only target market, so this is a caveat on the report's wording, not a defect to block on.

reasonText() only maps 'invalid-url'; any other Ack.reason is passed through raw, so a failure would render as a Greek prefix plus an English machine token (e.g. 'Δεν εφαρμόστηκε: untrusted-sender') — the same partial-localization class the finding is about. Currently unreachable from this page: the only two acked bridge calls are setServerUrl (returns just 'invalid-url', main.ts:340-346) and retry (always ok, main.ts:492-496), and isTrustedSender trusts file:// so DENIED cannot fire here. It becomes user-visible only if a future handler returns a new reason code.

When Chromium supplies no errorDescription the shell still synthesizes the English literal `error ${errorCode}` and hands it to the page, where it appears after the localized 'Τεχνική λεπτομέρεια:' label (confirmed in the VM run: 'Τεχνική λεπτομέρεια: https://x/ — error -105'). It sits in the deliberately-technical support line rather than in the message, so the finding's substance is still addressed, but one English word survives on the Greek page.

loadFallback now evaluates mainWindow.webContents.getURL() as the second locale source, and the render-process-gone path always reaches it (appOrigin has an empty pathname, so localeFromUrl returns null and the ?? does not short-circuit). The call is outside any try/catch, so if getURL() ever threw on a post-crash WebContents the fallback screen would not load at all and the user would be left on a blank window. In practice mainWindow.isDestroyed() is checked first and a crashed renderer does not destroy the WebContents, so I could not construct a failing case — flagged as a robustness note, not a demonstrated break.

verify.overall: frontend-09 is genuinely fixed and the fix survives packaging. I attacked the three things most likely to make an i18n fix fake — strings defined but never applied, a hardcoded or unreachable locale source, and a catalog path that only exists in the dev tree — and all three held up under execution rather than inspection: the fallback page's script was run in a VM across el/en, unreachable/crashed, four ERR_ classes, a bogus lang, no params, and no bridge, and every visible string plus all three click-handler statuses resolved correctly with Greek as the safe default; uiLocale() was exercised against six OS-locale/env combinations and localeFromUrl() against nine URLs; and the compiled output confirms dist/i18n.js is emitted as CommonJS and shipped by electron-builder's files list, with the page strings inline so the file:// document needs no filesystem or network access. tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0 and prettier --check are all clean, and check:translations is untouched because nothing was added to /locales. The four residual items are all low: a third-OS-locale menu still mixes Electron's role labels with Greek custom labels (no worse than before), one unreachable raw-reason passthrough, one English `error -105` string inside the deliberately-technical support line, and an unguarded getURL() in the crash path that I could not make throw. The untouched DEFAULT_APP_URL matches the audit's own downgrade of that half of the finding. No blockers; nothing here should stop the remediation being marked done.
